name: St. Petersburg Clearwater International Airport
before:
The quieter way into the Tampa Bay area, in Pinellas County, 9 miles north of downtown St Petersburg, 7 miles south east of Clearwater and 17 miles south west of Tampa.

It is a small airport and that is the point. One terminal with two gate areas, easy to move through, and it markets itself as "Tampa Bay The Easy Way". For a client staying on the Gulf beaches it is closer than flying into Tampa, though the route map is far smaller, so check what actually flies before assuming it works.

It is also home to Coast Guard Air Station Clearwater, the largest and busiest Coast Guard air station in the United States.

There are two runways, the longer at 9,730 feet with an instrument approach, on a 1,900 acre site.
after:
The quieter way into the Tampa Bay area, in Pinellas County, 9 miles north of downtown St Petersburg, 7 miles south east of Clearwater and 17 miles south west of Tampa.

It is a small airport and that is the point: one terminal, easy to move through. The route map is mostly Allegiant's, to US cities, so check what actually flies before assuming it works.

It is also home to Coast Guard Air Station Clearwater, the largest and busiest air station in the US Coast Guard.

There are two runways, the longer at 9,730 feet with an instrument approach.

claims.note: The FAA master record gives the distance from the central business district of its associated city, St Petersburg-Clearwater, as 8 nautical miles north, which is 9.2 statute miles; north rules out Clearwater, which lies north west of the airport. The coordinates check could not test this figure: GeoNames spells the city 'St. Petersburg', so geo.mjs fell back to Pinellas Park and its CHECK line does not apply. Other figures measure from somewhere else: the operator's directions page says '4 miles north of St. Petersburg' and Wikipedia's own history section 'six miles north of St. Petersburg', neither from downtown. Both agree on north.
